submitter: bugs_open/380 session — config slice (migrations 597, 598, 600, 601; 599 HELD for an owner plaintext read), 2026-08-24
rationale: bugs_open/380: three mechanisms fail OPEN on one condition. When a site's evidence_base has no facts, (a) build-site-planner tells the writer to use plain-string sections ('no facts keys'), so the writer's strong facts_scoped arm never fires; (b) page-content-writer has NO no-register arm at all — the Verified Facts block renders empty; (c) claims-auditor's check_opted_in branches on evidence_facts.facts_text (a string_agg over facts[], NULL for BOTH no register and an empty one) to else_step 'complete' — a skipped audit recorded as success. 33 of 48 sites are in that population [MEASURED 2026-08-24]. The writer is therefore freest exactly where it knows least: garden-tools.uk (greenfield, no register) shipped a 1,486-word review methodology for a business that has never tested a product ('Where we can, we buy the tool at the same price a reader would pay'; 'We garden ourselves, and we test what we can get our hands on'), and loanzy.uk shipped an invented credit broker. The auditor is additionally an ORPHAN: no seed file (migration 350 records it), no scheduled task, no spawner, ONE llm_call_log row in its life (2026-07-18, returned []) and a request_claims_review step that had never fired (item_key LIKE 'claims_llm%' = 0 rows, both figures pinned to before 2026-08-24 16:00Z). This was first diagnosed 2026-07-20 (claims_verification/PLAN_2026-07-20_gaswholesalers_second_site.md §3, the unbuilt 'cold_audit' posture). RULINGS APPLIED: RFC_017 (owner 2026-08-08: audits fail CLOSED — a DB error now FAILS the run instead of completing it); RFC_023 (owner 2026-08-12: making a failure visible is a fix, ordinary gate — no consumer's success path changes: the auditor had no consumer, and the planner/writer edits are prompt narrowings with no new template variables); owner 2026-08-24 on this bug ('aspirations stated as present-tense practice… say only what is sourced, and source more' — NOT 'write less'); owner decisions taken in-session today: D1 NO empty register is minted or backfilled (absence IS the cold posture — a shell register parses to nil, CLM-005, and reads as protection it is not; answers RFC_003 §8 Q2 'no'); D2 rotation 3600s tick / 7-day window; D4 the writer arm is HELD (_HOLD + committed v5 plaintext) until the owner reads it, because RFC_016 §5.2 voids the 2026-08-09 v4 approval on any edit. WHAT SHIPS: 597 deletes check_opted_in, repoints load_evidence_facts to load_page_text, removes its error_step, adds a cold-register prompt arm ({{if .evidence_facts.facts_text}} roster {{else}} report practice/possession/track-record/named-relationship assertions at high/medium/low with an explicit do-not-report list for could-framed, negated, quoted and industry statements), nil-guards ALLOWED ENTITIES, raises the per-page text cap 3500→12000, declares recurrence_expected:false on request_claims_review (migration 572's reasoning — the two-strike revalidator contract is unchanged), and writes ONE doc_notes receipt per run (pipeline/claims-audit, audit-ran|audit-findings — the RFC_022/RFC_024 convention: a MISSING row means it did not run). 598 makes the planner's two identical {{else}} arms distinct, both mandating the OBJECT form with "facts": [] on every section (proven end to end with no Go change: scopeItem scopes a non-nil empty list; every carrier keeps [] distinct from NULL; the section_facts wire is live on page-build-handler), the no-register arm adding a no-operating-history planning rule; rule 17's contradictory last sentence edited in the same migration. 600 gives the auditor a clock (590's rotation template, shipped-page predicate, locked_at IS NULL, stamp in site_discovery_rotation). 601 is the follow-up the first live proof found: the auditor's page-text extraction was eating most of every multi-component page because a PostgreSQL ARE regex takes the greediness of its FIRST quantifier — '<style[^>]*>.*?</style>' is greedy as a whole and, over a string_agg with no ORDER BY, matched first-<style>-to-last-</style> across components; the owner's own quoted sentence reached the model NOWHERE (position('we buy')=0 in the rendered prompt). Fix: strip per component, lazy first quantifier, deterministic order; measured 8,266 chars with the sentence present vs 3,732 without. A seed for claims-auditor is committed for the first time, regenerated from the post-601 live row. LIVE PROOF: 597 hand-dispatched at garden-tools.uk (corr 86ef3e17): cold arm rendered, findings returned ('We test and research carefully', high), the first claims_llm_* work item in the step's life filed, receipt written; control at leopardessconsulting.co.uk (corr be39ddba): roster arm rendered, one real drift finding ('22 sites' vs verified floor 25). Re-dispatched after 601 (corr bcf23316) as the demand control for the sentence.

edits.rationale: [MODIFY — APPLIED ~17:25Z, recorded; verify block ran the motivating extraction live: how-we-assess 8,266 chars, sentence present=t] Found by the first live proof: all six page rows reached the prompt but how-we-assess's faq component text — with the owner's quoted sentence — did not; index stripped to ONE char. Not a tag problem (every component's <style> pairs balance). PostgreSQL ARE: a regex takes the greediness of its FIRST quantified atom, so '<style[^>]*>.*?</style>' is greedy as a whole and, over a string_agg with no ORDER BY, matches first-<style>-to-last-</style> across components. Fix: strip each component alone (one style block each), lazy first quantifier, deterministic ORDER BY pc.position, pc.slot_name. Fleet census: this SQL shape exists on exactly one live agent (the two Go rerender actions use RE2, which has no such rule).
edits.sketch: LEFT(regexp_replace(string_agg(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(pc.rendered_html, '<style[^>]*?>.*?</style>', ' ', 'gi'), '<script[^>]*?>.*?</script>', ' ', 'gi'), '<[^>]*>', ' ', 'g'), ' ' ORDER BY pc.position, pc.slot_name), '\s+', ' ', 'g'), 12000) AS page_text
